title: Minimum Steiner tree

problem.name: Minimum Steiner tree
problem.statement_latex:
Given an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$, nonnegative edge weights $w$, and terminals $R\subseteq V$, $|R|=k$, find a connected subgraph containing $R$ of minimum total weight. An optimum may be chosen as a tree. Steiner vertices permit cheaper network connections than restricting the tree to terminals.
The quantum bound uses QRAM time, while classical bounds count RAM operations with the stated weight-arithmetic costs.
problem.statement_text: Given an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$, nonnegative edge weights $w$, and terminals $R\subseteq V$, $|R|=k$, find a connected subgraph containing $R$ of minimum total weight. An optimum may be chosen as a tree. Steiner vertices permit cheaper network connections than restricting the tree to terminals. The quantum bound uses QRAM time, while classical bounds count RAM operations with the stated weight-arithmetic costs.

quantum.details_latex: The exponential parameter is the number $k$ of terminals, while polynomial factors include graph size and weight arithmetic. The construction uses a recurrence based on splitting a Steiner tree, together with partial preprocessing and nested quantum minimum finding. Its table values must be coherently accessible.
quantum.details_text: The exponential parameter is the number $k$ of terminals, while polynomial factors include graph size and weight arithmetic. The construction uses a recurrence based on splitting a Steiner tree, together with partial preprocessing and nested quantum minimum finding. Its table values must be coherently accessible.

classical.headline_latex: $(2+\delta)^k n^{f(1/\delta)}$ for fixed $\delta>0$, M\"olle--Richter--Rossmanith; $O^*(2^k)$ for bounded integer weights, subset convolution.
classical.details_latex: The subset-convolution bound includes the dependence on the weight range. These improve the $O^*(3^k)$ Dreyfus--Wagner recurrence and the $O^*(2.684^k)$ splitting algorithm. For unit-weight sparse graphs, Gaspers' path-decomposition methods give vertex-parameter bounds $O^*(1.1661^n)$ on degree-three graphs and $O^*(1.3100^n)$ on degree-four graphs, using exponential memory. On such inputs the appropriate comparator is the minimum of the applicable terminal- and vertex-parameter bounds.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant in terminal count in the general comparison, using amplitude amplification. Sparse unit-weight regimes also have the stated classical vertex-parameter bounds.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous QRAM upper bound and partial evidence against the strongest displayed classical algorithms in the relevant weight and graph regimes.

hardware.description_latex: Polynomial active registers encode terminal subsets, vertices, costs and reconstruction data, together with exponential coherent preprocessing memory. Useful terminal counts require fault tolerance; graph and weight parameters affect the polynomial register and arithmetic costs.

algorithm_items.content_latex: \href{https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.03581}{Miyamoto, Iwamura, Kise and Le Gall, \emph{Quantum Speedup for the Minimum Steiner Tree Problem} (2019/2020)}. Theorem 1; Section 3.1 defines Dreyfus--Wagner, Section 3.2 gives the splitting recurrence, and Section 4 gives the quantum algorithm. Table 1 and its cited classical papers specify the weight-dependent comparisons.
